court.label: Your half, seen from above. Net at the top.

learn.heading: Explore the rotation
learn.rotationInfo: Rotation 1: the setter is in position 1. Each side-out moves you one rotation on (setter in 6, 5, 4, 3, 2).

notes.1: Setter serves from position 1. Three front-row attackers — the strongest attack rotation.
notes.2: Setter is front right next to the net. Only two front-row attackers.
notes.3: Setter is middle front and slides right to the net. Two front-row attackers.
notes.4: Setter is front left and has the longest way to the target area. Two front-row attackers.
notes.5: Setter is back left, releases to the net from deep. Three front-row attackers.
notes.6: Setter is middle back. Three front-row attackers, setter runs through the middle.

quiz.heading: Practise formations

instruction.serve: Your team serves. Drag every player into a legal formation — position 1 stands behind the end line.
instruction.receive: The opponent serves. Drag every player into a legal serve-receive formation.
instruction.base: The ball is passed. Drag every player to their base position for the attack: setter to the target at the net, hitters to their approach spots, libero and back-row outside behind.

legend.serve: The dashed area behind the end line is the service zone. Only position 1 may stand there and is exempt from overlap with 2 and 6.
legend.receive: Line under the number: passers (libero, or the back-row middle without one, and both outsides). The opposite and the setter do not pass; a front-row middle stays at the net.
legend.base: No need to be pixel-perfect: a player counts as correct when close enough to the base position.

quiz.keyboardHint: Keyboard: select a player, move with the arrow keys, confirm with Enter.
quiz.explanationOkServe: No overlap at the moment of the serve. Position 1 stands behind the end line in the service zone.
quiz.explanationOkReceive: No overlap at the moment of the serve. The setter hides and runs to the net after contact.
quiz.explanationBad: Not quite. The marked pairs overlap — the shadow shows a legal example.

hint.serve: Front row closer to the net than the back row, left stays left of right. The server stands behind the end line.
hint.receive: A front-row player must be closer to the net than the player directly behind, and left stays left of right — in both rows, including position 1. The server exception applies only when your own team serves.
hint.base: Setter right-side net, front row on the attack line (outside on the left pin, middle in the centre, opposite on the right), libero left back, back-row outside middle back.

reasons.front-behind-back: Position {{a}} must be closer to the net than position {{b}}.
reasons.front-row-order: In the front row, position {{a}} must stand left of position {{b}}.
reasons.back-row-order: In the back row, position {{a}} must stand left of position {{b}}.
reasons.server-not-in-zone: Position 1 must stand behind the end line in the service zone.

quiz.explanationBase: Correct: after the pass the setter runs to the target at the right-side net, the hitters step to the attack line for their approach, the libero stands left back.
quiz.explanationBaseBad: At least one player is still too far from their base position. Fix the marked players — the shadow shows the base position.

onboarding.step1Body: You look at your own half from above, the net is at the top. Position 1 is right back and serves; 4, 3, 2 are the front row.
onboarding.step2Body: In the 5-1 there is one setter, one opposite, two outsides and two middles. Players with the same job always stand three positions apart.
onboarding.step3Body: After a side-out everyone moves one position clockwise: 1 → 6 → 5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1. Rotation 1 means the setter is in position 1; each side-out is the next rotation.
